verses.text: When David finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan felt deeply bound to David and loved him as he loved himself.
From that day Saul kept David with him and no longer let him go back to his father's house.
Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as he loved himself.
Jonathan took off his robe and gave it to David, along with his clothes, sword, bow, and belt.
David went wherever Saul sent him and acted wisely. Saul put him in charge of fighting men, and this pleased both the people and Saul's servants.
When David came back from killing the Philistine, women from all over Israel came out to greet King Saul. They sang and danced with tambourines and other instruments, celebrating.
As they played, the women sang to one another, “Saul has killed his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
Saul was furious. He said, “They've given David credit for tens of thousands and me for just thousands. What more can he get except the kingdom?”
From then on Saul kept a suspicious eye on David.
The next day an evil spirit from God came powerfully over Saul, and he prophesied inside the house. David played as he did every day, and Saul held a spear.
Saul hurled the spear, thinking, “I'll pin David to the wall.” David escaped him twice.
Saul was afraid of David because the LORD was with David and had left Saul.
So Saul sent David away from his presence and put him in command of a thousand men. David led the troops out and brought them back.
David acted wisely in everything he did, and the LORD was with him.
When Saul saw how wisely David acted, he became even more afraid of him.
All Israel and Judah loved David because he led them out and brought them back.

Saul told David, “Here's my older daughter Merab. I'll give her to you as your wife. Just be brave in my service and fight the LORD's battles.” Saul was thinking, “I'll let the Philistines kill him so I don't have to.”
David asked, “Who am I, and what standing do I or my father's family have in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?”
When the time came for Saul's daughter Merab to marry David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite instead.
Saul's daughter Michal loved David. When Saul heard, the news pleased him.
He thought, “I'll give her to David, and she'll become a trap for him. Then the Philistines can get him.” So Saul told David a second time, “Today you'll become my son-in-law.”
Saul told his servants to speak privately to David and say, “The king likes you, and all his servants love you. Now go ahead and become his son-in-law.”
When the servants told David, he replied, “Do you think becoming the king's son-in-law is a small thing? I'm poor and hardly anyone knows me.”
Saul's servants reported what David had said.
Saul said, “Tell David the king asks for no bride price except a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.” Saul hoped the Philistines would kill David.
When the servants told David, he was pleased at the chance to become the king's son-in-law. Before the deadline,

David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. David brought back their foreskins and gave the full number to the king to become his son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.
Saul saw that the LORD was with David and knew that his daughter Michal loved him.
Saul became even more afraid of David, and from then on he was always David's enemy.
Whenever the Philistine commanders came out to fight, David acted more wisely than all Saul's other officers. His name became widely respected.
